name: Ed Markey

issue_poll.name: UMass Amherst Poll of Massachusetts registered voters (YouGov), Aug. 5-12, 2026: single most important issue for state leaders to address
issue_poll.note: Statewide poll that ranks issues; question asks what Gov. Healey and the Legislature should address, not the Senate vote specifically. Order by share: cost of living 39, housing 14, immigration 11, health care 9, taxes 9, transportation and infrastructure 4, climate change 4, homelessness 3, crime 2, education 2 (ties kept in the poll's listed order). Closer polls checked: UMass Lowell (Oct. 7-18, 2026) and Suffolk/Boston Globe (June 2026) had no issue-ranking question in available text.

issues.detail: Raise federal minimum wage to $17 (Raise the Wage Act), indexed to inflation; national paid family and medical leave.
Pass Green New Deal for Public Housing Act (up to $234B over 10 years, repeal Faircloth Amendment); national just-cause eviction standard.
Pass DREAM Act and path to citizenship; abolish ICE; end detention bed quota; vote no on any DHS funding; ban masked agents.
Pass Medicare for All; cap Medicare Advantage payments at traditional Medicare rates; pass Health Over Wealth Act; repeal Hyde Amendment.
2% annual tax on net worth $50M-$1B plus 1% surtax above $1B; close carried interest loophole; make expanded Child Tax Credit permanent.
Pass Freedom to Move Act for fare-free public transit nationwide; phase out new gas and diesel vehicle sales by 2035.
100% clean energy by 2035; ban new federal coal, oil and gas leases; reverse halt of Massachusetts offshore wind projects.
Pass Housing ACCESS Act to expand supportive housing; bar federal police from arresting unhoused people on federal land absent alternatives.
Reinstate assault weapons ban; ban high-capacity magazines; repeal gun industry liability shield (PLCAA); end qualified immunity.
Pass No Cuts to Public Schools Act; fully fund IDEA; universal free school meals; raise TEACH Grant to $8,000; tuition-free public college.

plan_caveats: Nearly all positions come from Markey's 2026 Progressive Massachusetts endorsement questionnaire (many items are YES answers to listed proposals); his campaign site issue page, rallies, town halls and the Oct. 13, 2026 Deaton debate stated mostly general goals ('lower costs', 'lower housing costs', Medicare for All, Green New Deal).
Questionnaire completion date not shown on the page; it is labeled the 2026 Congressional Endorsement Questionnaire for U.S. Senate.

Offshore wind reversal in Climate comes from WBUR coverage of the Oct. 13, 2026 debate (https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/10/14/senate-markey-deaton-debate-trump-healthcare-energy-massachusetts), not the questionnaire.

Issue poll asks about priorities for state government, not the Senate race; used because it is the latest 2026 Massachusetts poll found that ranks issues. Homelessness (3%) listed separately from housing as the poll did.
Past bills he cites as accomplishments (e.g., INTERDICT Act, Fair Share Amendment, E-Rate) are record and not counted; only forward-looking support counted.
